correctness.rationale: The birth–death order-preserving coupling and path Kantorovich formula reduce the induced W1 norm exactly to the maximum of adjacent positive gradients of P_t x. Reflection about the slow edge identifies its central gradient as 2e₀ᵀexp(tR_ε)z, R_ε=R₀−2εe₀e₀ᵀ. Neumann cosine eigenvectors give the ε=0 expansion; analytic perturbation of the separated slow mode gives eigenvalue 2ε/m and amplitude m−(m−1)²ε/2+O(ε²). The first fast decay has λ_m and B=(2/m)cot²(π/(2m)), satisfying Bλ_m/2=K_m. Uniform control of the interior-edge stable spectrum rules out their dominance for small ε. Balancing slow decay 2εt against fast deficit Be^(−λ_m t) localizes the global peak at log(K_m/ε)/λ_m and yields the second-order coefficient. The small-time central gradient derivative equals 2(1−ε), and at ε=1 the Dirichlet gradient generator is substochastic. Independently constructed full 2m×2m generators confirmed peak/time asymptotics over m=2..6 at ε=10^−4,10^−6. Finite numerics do not prove the spectral uniformity assertions.
